**Late-Cycle / Transition Risk.** The US is in a **late-cycle, growth-softening regime** where residual nominal strength (inflation sticky at 3.7% PCE, ISM Manufacturing at 55.6) masks deteriorating labor momentum (NFP -23K in July), a slowing Q2 GDP print of just 1.5%, a 3m10y curve still inverted with a >30% model-implied recession probability, and a Fed that is effectively on hold at a real policy rate that remains **above neutral** — the June dot plot median of 3.375% against a long-run neutral of ~3% means real rates are still mildly restrictive against sticky inflation. The 35bps gap between the dot plot median and market pricing creates a fragility point: if PCE re-accelerates toward 4%, the market must reprice the Fed hold as a hike signal, compressing multiples sharply on the long-duration growth trade.

A rebound toward +100K+ confirms AI-driven productivity restructuring; a second consecutive negative print shifts the conversation from "soft landing" to recession and would likely see a sharp steepening of the curve and rotation into defensives.

Investors are assessing the Treasury's plan to at least double its buybacks, with Stanley Druckenmiller publicly arguing the move undermines Treasury market credibility
